question: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are separated by which water body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten Degree Channel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Ten Degree Channel** is a water body that separates the **Andaman Islands** from the **Nicobar Islands**. It is located in the Bay of Bengal and plays a significant role in defining the geographical distinction between these two island groups.
 
• The channel is approximately **150 kilometers wide** and lies between the **Little Andaman Island** (part of the Andaman group) and the **Car Nicobar Island** (part of the Nicobar group).
 
• The name "Ten Degree Channel" is derived from its location near the **10° North latitude**, which is a significant geographical marker.
 
• It is an important maritime route in the Bay of Bengal and serves as a natural bound
